howto.name: Choose a video or recording
howto.text: Drop or choose a video or recording. Most MP4, MOV, M4A, WebM and MKV files, and MP3 and WAV, are read a minute at a time, up to 3 hours of sound however big the video is. Ogg, Opus, FLAC and AAC files, and MP4s written in fragments, are decoded whole, up to 15 minutes. The file is read in this browser and is not uploaded.

howto.name: Choose the language and the model
howto.text: Pick the language spoken in the file: this browser version of Whisper does not work it out. Whisper Base, about 74 MB, is the more accurate; Tiny, about 41 MB, is faster and needs less memory. The model downloads from Hugging Face on the first run and your browser keeps it.

howto.name: Choose how the captions look
howto.text: Two lines of up to 42 characters suit players, TV and YouTube; one line of 42, or one short line of 24 for vertical video. Chinese, Japanese and Korean lines hold 16 characters, or 10 when short. No caption stays up longer than 7 seconds.

howto.name: Generate the subtitles
howto.text: Click Generate subtitles. The bar shows how far through the sound Whisper has got and the time left at the speed so far; Stop keeps the captions written up to that point.

howto.name: Check, correct and download
howto.text: Play the file with the captions on it and correct any words; clear a caption to leave it out. Then download SRT or VTT, named after your file. Add Subtitles can burn the SRT into the video, which uploads the video and the subtitles to PrivaTools for temporary processing.

faq.a: No. The sound is read from the file and turned into subtitles in your browser, and the video or recording is not sent to PrivaTools or anyone else. What is downloaded is the Whisper model from Hugging Face and the engine that runs it from jsDelivr, once; your browser keeps them, and AI Studio shows the model's size and can remove it.

faq.q: Is it free, and is there a watermark?
faq.a: It is free, with no account, no watermark and no limit on how many files you subtitle. The subtitles are plain SRT or VTT text files that you can edit anywhere.

Good on clear speech from one person at a time. Music, people talking over each other, strong accents, poor microphones and unusual names cause mistakes, and Tiny makes more than Base. Tiny also sometimes stops writing before the speech ends: when clear speech follows its last caption, the tool asks it again from there and keeps each line of that only when it reads as speech, so a line can still be missed. Over music Whisper can write a word or a stock line such as "Thank you."; one it writes over silence is left out. Where it writes the same words over and over, that stretch is heard again, and left out if it still repeats, with the result saying where; a short chant or refrain stays as it was said, but a long one can make Whisper write the same words over and over, and is then handled like any other loop. Read the captions while the file plays before you publish them.

faq.q: Which languages does it work with?
faq.a: Whisper's 99 languages. Choose the one spoken in the file: this browser version does not detect it, and the wrong choice gives garbled or translated captions. It writes best in widely spoken languages such as English, Spanish, French and German, and much less well in languages with little training data, especially with Tiny.

Whisper runs on your own processor, so it depends on the device. On a two-core test machine, Base took about 45 seconds per minute of speech and Tiny about 20; most laptops are faster, phones slower. The page shows how far it has got and the time left at the speed so far, and the tab has to stay open.

faq.q: How long can the video be, and how much memory does it need?
faq.a: Up to 3 hours of sound. Most MP4, MOV, M4A, WebM and MKV files, and MP3 and WAV, are read about a minute at a time, so a long file needs no more memory for its sound than a short one; Ogg, Opus, FLAC and AAC files, and MP4s written in fragments, are decoded whole, up to 15 minutes. Whisper needs memory of its own while it runs: in our tests in Chromium, the tab used about 1 to 2 GB with Tiny and about 2 GB with Base, so choose Tiny on a phone.

faq.q: Why are some captions early or late?
faq.a: Whisper times each stretch of speech it writes, but coarsely. The tool moves the change from one stretch to the next into the pause between them, then draws each caption in to where the sound actually is, from a tenth of a second before the first word to a quarter of a second after the last. Next to music or steady noise there is no silence to measure, and Whisper can start a caption where the music starts, many seconds before the words. A caption far longer than its words take to say is shortened to about the time they take, kept to its end that borders a pause, which brings most within a second or two of the voice; a caption can still show over music before the words.

faq.q: What is the difference between SRT and VTT?
faq.a: SRT (SubRip) is the most widely read: video editors, VLC, YouTube and most social sites take it. VTT (WebVTT) is the format web players load through the HTML track element. Both hold the same words and timings.

faq.q: How do I add the subtitles to my video?
faq.a: Upload the SRT next to the video where you publish it, since YouTube, Vimeo and most social sites take one, or load it in your player; a file named like the video is easier for players to find. To burn the captions into the picture so they show everywhere, use Add Subtitles, which uploads the video and the subtitles to PrivaTools for temporary processing.

faq.q: What if my file doesn't work?
faq.a: The browser has to decode the sound itself. When it can't, because of an unusual codec, an AVI file or a damaged file, the tool says so and nothing is sent anywhere. Extract Audio can make an MP3 of an MP4, MOV, WebM, AVI or MKV video's sound, and Audio Converter of a WAV, OGG, FLAC, AAC, M4A or WMA recording, both on the PrivaTools server, which means uploading the file, up to 200 MB, for temporary processing; the MP3 then works here.

faq.q: Can it translate the subtitles into another language?
faq.a: Not by itself: it writes what is said, in the language it is said in. To translate the subtitles, download the SRT, open Subtitle Translator and choose the downloaded file.
